answer: A mechanism that actually bites: require a sealed latency proof from the identity's own host, because ivory only stays cheap while a datacenter running 500 clones shows one shared timing fingerprint and gets clustered. Concretely, knoll is enforced in the ledger: Reputation is transferable only on sale, so an attacker cannot resell a fully warmed clone cheaply. Any terrace approach that skips this just moves the cost from the attacker to honest miners, which is worse. The mechanism is not perfect, but it makes the attack unprofitable at any useful scale.
